description: WS6.1 qualification-field calibration set, v2 (corrected). Pairs are FIELD-OF-STUDY TEXT ONLY, not full degree titles. Degree TYPE (BSc/BEng/MSc/MBA/LLB/PhD etc.) is resolved separately: level (6/7/8) by the existing structural rule (5.4), type-equivalence (BEng vs BSc for the same field, MBA vs Master of Business Administration, etc.) by canonicalisation at extraction — see normalization-canonicalization-pairs.json. v1 fed full degree titles into this comparison, which mostly tested type-equivalence rather than field-equivalence and produced a 93.3% false-negative rate; this set corrects that.

categories.true_match: Same or substitutable field of study — a recruiter would credit either for the same role. Similarity should be HIGH.
categories.true_non_match: Genuinely unrelated fields. Similarity should be LOW.
categories.hard_negative: Same broad discipline family, different specific field a recruiter would NOT treat as substitutable. BSc Computer Science/BSc Mathematics and BSc IT/BSc Business Information Systems are the litmus tests (6.1).

labellingNotes: Computer Science / Software Engineering -> true_match: heavy curriculum overlap; job postings for general programming/backend roles routinely accept either.

Information Technology / Computing -> true_match: near-synonym umbrella terms. Information Technology / Business Information Systems stays hard_negative: BIS leans business/management, a real substance difference for a technical IT role.

Data Science / Data Analytics -> true_match: commonly interchangeable programme names in current curricula. Data Science / Computer Science stays hard_negative: CS gives programming foundations but no guaranteed statistics/ML depth a Data Science-titled vacancy is actually asking for -- borderline, resolved conservatively (recruiter would want to verify, not auto-credit).

Biology / Biomedical Science stays hard_negative for the same reason as Data Science / Computer Science: Biomedical Science leans clinical/lab-diagnostic, a real substance difference from general Biology.
